title: Completion unit compatibility on good integral representatives
statement: Let l be prime, E/Q_l finite, and h:U→T arbitrary. Fix a:PbcProperIntegralPullbackIdentification l E h and an isomorphism b of the transported completed pullback with the actual pulled strict quotient tower derived limit, and assume PbcProperIntegralModelMatching l E h a b [def-weil-pbc-proper-integral-ordinary-data]. For every P in integralOperationsGoodComplex l E T (a flat-term K-flat complex), transport of the ordinaryIntegralCompletionComparison component at DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj followed by b.hom at that object equals a.derivedIso.hom there followed by completedPullbackComparison h (pbcIntegralDatum l E) at the transport of that object. Both a and b are inputs. This asserts the identity only on the specified resolving representatives, without constructing either comparison or extending it to arbitrary derived objects.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4), Remark 6.8.15; Stacks sites-cohomology.tex lemma-derived-limit-is-ok (Tag 0941), proetale.tex Tag 099N(5)

proof.text: Choose the functorial entire-tower K-injective resolution with injective terms. Unpack model matching at P and this resolution to obtain t, z and iota. Build the termwise-limit cone and its canonical isomorphism to the limit in complexes. Product and mapping-cocone extensionality identify iota with this isomorphism followed by the standard Roos inclusion. Exact countable products and strictRoosDerivation make it a quasi-isomorphism. Thus the actual tower counit, localized resolution, universal Rlim computation and localized iota form an invertible postcomposition.

Let j be the cochain isomorphism induced by a.moduleIso and c=j inverse followed by coefficient transport of ordinaryIntegralCompletionChain and z. Expand the first and second coordinate equations of z. Functoriality of scalar restriction, the ordinary mapping-cocone lift formulas and t augmentation normalization show that c has the actual quotient augmentation in every first product projection and zero second coordinate. This calculation is in complexes before localization. The proved coordinate theorem supplies the transported augmentation and its chain equality, separately compiled to keep the concrete conversions small.

Cancel the invertible postcomposition from the desired identity. The model matching equation rewrites b. The defining good-representative normalization of ordinaryIntegralCompletionComparison rewrites eta; naturality of the coefficient localization factor moves the ordinary chain map through that factor. Apply actual-unit Roos normalization to c. The derived_counit equation of a identifies the two ordinary computation maps. Finally Q(j) Q(c)=Q(transported ordinary chain) Q(z), since j j inverse is the identity. Reassociate and conclude.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 099N(5), lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case. Formal coordinate transport and cancellation written by K7; the remaining actual-unit normalization is separated from integral-model matching.

lean.statement:
theorem pbc_integral_completion_matching_on_good
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra ℚ_[l] E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℚ_[l] E] {U T : Scheme.{u}} (h : U ⟶ T)
    (a : PbcProperIntegralPullbackIdentification l E h)
    (b : integralDerivedPullback l E h ⋙ integralDetailedTransport U l E ≅
      integralDetailedTransport T l E ⋙ completedReductionTower T (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
        completedTowerPullback h (pbcIntegralDatum l E) ⋙
          completedTowerRlim (pbcIntegralDatum l E) U)
    (hm : PbcProperIntegralModelMatching l E h a b)
    (P : (integralOperationsGoodComplex l E T).FullSubcategory) :
      (integralDetailedTransport U l E).map
          ((ordinaryIntegralCompletionComparison l E h).app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj)) ≫
          b.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) =
        a.derivedIso.hom.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj) ≫
          completedPullbackComparison h (pbcIntegralDatum l E)
            ((integralDetailedTransport T l E).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P.obj))
